headline: AI, IoT, and Critical Infrastructure Under Fire: Daily Cybersecurity Brief
summary: This daily cybersecurity summary highlights significant updates and new threats impacting various sectors.  The TuxBot v3 framework, developed with LLM assistance, has evolved with Kimwolf v7 targeting Android IoT devices and employing sophisticated DDoS attacks.  Miasma and Hades worms continue their supply chain attacks, with a major breach of the LiteLLM AI framework exposing cloud credentials and API keys, affecting thousands of organizations.  US water utilities are facing widespread cyberattacks from Iran-linked actors, with new reports detailing disruptions to communication systems and exploitation of Rockwell devices via internet-exposed PLCs.  The COLDCARD wallet RNG flaw has led to an estimated $100-130 million in Bitcoin theft due to a critical reduction in seed phrase entropy.  Unlimited Technology Systems experienced a ransomware attack in October 2025, leading to the exfiltration of 3.8 million patient records and a subsequent class-action lawsuit due to delayed notification.  The 'RovoBlast' flaw in Atlassian AI, while not yet exploited in the wild, enabled one-click data exfiltration via a 'Parameter-to-Prompt' injection technique, potentially affecting Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.  Storm-1175 is exploiting an N-able flaw (CVE-2026-18577) for post-compromise activities including network discovery and credential dumping, prompting a second hotfix from N-able.  New threats include the Lazarus Group exploiting a Windows zero-day (CVE-2026-68820) in espionage campaigns targeting defense and aerospace.  CISA warns of the Gunra RaaS, derived from Conti, targeting critical infrastructure with double extortion tactics.  The DentaQuest breach has impacted 15 million individuals, becoming the largest healthcare breach of 2026, with ShinyHunters claiming responsibility.  A Polish power plant was breached via a private cellular APN network, with attackers pivoting through a compromised wind farm to gain access.  Lennar Corp. disclosed a social engineering data breach affecting an undisclosed number of individuals.  Oculus Pathology experienced a breach via employee email accounts, potentially exposing patient PII and PHI.  Finally, the Aeternum botnet is utilizing the Polygon blockchain for resilient C2 infrastructure, making takedowns extremely difficult.

articles.headline: TuxBot v3: New IoT Botnet Framework Developed with LLM Assistance
articles.title: TuxBot v3 IoT Botnet Uses LLMs for Code Generation
articles.excerpt: Security researchers have uncovered TuxBot v3 Evolution, a modular Internet of Things (IoT) botnet framework partially developed using a large language model (LLM). The malware, analyzed by Unit 42, is derived from the AISURU and Wuhan botnet families and targets IoT devices for Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks. Its primary infection vector is brute-forcing Telnet credentials. While the LLM-assisted development introduced several non-functional components and bugs, the core infection and DDoS capabilities are operational. The framework's source code indicates a connection to an Iranian developer and shared infrastructure with the Keksec/Kaitori malware family, highlighting a significant and evolving threat to IoT device security.
articles.updateSummary: Kimwolf v7, a variant of the AISURU botnet family, introduces advanced HTTP/2 DDoS and resilient C2 via Ethereum Name Service and Tor, targeting Android IoT devices.
articles.updateContent: Unit 42 reports Kimwolf v7, an evolution of the AISURU botnet family, now targets Android-based IoT devices via ADB exploitation. This variant features a sophisticated HTTP/2-based DDoS flood that mimics legitimate browser traffic, making detection and mitigation more challenging. Its command and control (C2) infrastructure has been significantly enhanced for resilience, utilizing the Ethereum Name Service (ENS) for primary C2 resolution and a Tor .onion address as a fallback. These advancements represent a direct response to previous C2 takedown efforts, increasing the botnet's operational durability and overall threat level.

articles.headline: Miasma and Hades Worms Continue Supply Chain Attacks on npm and PyPI
articles.title: Miasma, Hades Worms Target npm, PyPI
articles.excerpt: Self-propagating malware worms dubbed Miasma and Hades are continuing their assault on the npm and PyPI open-source ecosystems. Attributed to the financially motivated group TeamPCP, the worms spread by compromising developer accounts and publishing malicious new packages. The Hades variant, targeting PyPI, uses a novel technique involving `*-setup.pth` files to execute its payload, which harvests developer credentials and exfiltrates them to GitHub. The campaign has compromised over 100 packages, highlighting the significant and ongoing threat to the software supply chain.
articles.updateSummary: TeamPCP launched a major supply chain attack targeting LiteLLM, exposing over 2,500 companies and 434,000 CI/CD pipelines via malicious PyPI packages.
articles.updateContent: The ongoing TeamPCP campaign has escalated with a significant attack on the LiteLLM open-source AI framework. Malicious versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 were published to PyPI, designed to harvest cloud credentials, API keys for LLMs (OpenAI, Azure, Google), and cloud providers (AWS, GCP) from AI development environments. This incident, leveraging .pth files for execution, is considered the largest AI infrastructure breach of 2026, affecting over 2,500 organizations and 434,000 CI/CD pipelines. The FBI warns of long-term credential misuse.

articles.headline: Widespread Cyberattacks on US Water Utilities Prompt Federal Warning
articles.title: US Water Systems in 7 States Hit by Cyberattacks Targeting PLCs
articles.excerpt: Federal authorities, including the FBI and EPA, are investigating a wave of cyberattacks against water and wastewater facilities in at least seven U.S. states. The attacks, suspected to be linked to Iranian actors, target internet-exposed Rockwell Automation PLCs, causing operational disruptions like loss of water pressure and forcing utilities to switch to manual operations.
articles.updateSummary: Iran-linked cyberattacks on US water utilities now affect at least a dozen states, including NJ and AL. Phone system outages are reported; ports 44818 and 2222 are identified as targets.
articles.updateContent: The ongoing cyber campaign by Iran-linked actors targeting US water and wastewater facilities has expanded its scope. Initially reported in at least seven states, the attacks now affect at least a dozen states, with New Jersey and Alabama explicitly named as new victims. Beyond operational disruptions like pressure loss and flooding, new reports indicate disruptions to phone and communication systems. Technical details now highlight specific target ports 44818 (EtherNet/IP) and 2222 (Telnet/CLI) for Rockwell devices, emphasizing the exploitation of internet-exposed PLCs via default credentials and remotely accessible services.

articles.headline: COLDCARD Wallet RNG Flaw Linked to $88.6 Million Bitcoin Theft
articles.title: COLDCARD Wallet Flaw Suspected in $88.6M Bitcoin Theft
articles.excerpt: A firmware vulnerability in COLDCARD Bitcoin hardware wallets is the suspected cause of a theft totaling approximately $88.6 million in Bitcoin. The flaw, which caused the device to use a weak pseudorandom number generator (PRNG) for creating recovery seeds, allowed attackers to predict and reconstruct private keys. The theft occurred in automated sweeps just before the vulnerability was publicly disclosed. Users of affected devices are urged to generate new seeds on patched firmware and transfer their funds immediately, as simply updating the device does not secure existing, compromised wallets.
articles.updateSummary: Total stolen Bitcoin from Coldcard wallet flaw now exceeds $100M, with multiple hacking groups exploiting the vulnerability. New details reveal entropy reduced to 40 bits.
articles.updateContent: The estimated financial loss from the Coldcard wallet vulnerability has increased significantly, now ranging from $100 million to $130 million. Further technical analysis reveals the flaw, a build configuration error, critically reduced the seed phrase entropy from 128 bits to just 40 bits, making private key brute-forcing feasible. Exploitation is now attributed to multiple distinct hacking groups, indicating a broader attack surface and impact, including high-profile victims. This update highlights the escalating severity and wider scope of the incident.

articles.headline: Unlimited Technology Systems Breach Exposes 3.8M Patient Records
articles.title: Unlimited Technology Systems Breach Hits 3.8M
articles.excerpt: Unlimited Technology Systems, a healthcare revenue cycle management company, has disclosed a data breach affecting 3,803,750 individuals. The incident, which occurred in October 2025, involved an unauthorized actor accessing a commercial data center and potentially exfiltrating files containing a vast amount of patient data. Compromised information includes names, Social Security numbers, dates of birth, medical record numbers, diagnoses, and health insurance details. The company, a business associate for thousands of clinics, began notifying affected individuals in July 2026.
articles.updateSummary: New details reveal the breach was a ransomware attack with data exfiltration, leading to a class-action lawsuit due to the 9-month notification delay.
articles.updateContent: New information clarifies that the October 2025 incident at Unlimited Systems was a ransomware attack where an unauthorized actor accessed and exfiltrated sensitive patient data before deploying ransomware. This confirms a double extortion tactic, adding a critical technical detail to the initial report of unauthorized access. Furthermore, the significant nine-month delay in notifying the 3.8 million affected individuals has now resulted in a proposed class-action lawsuit against the company. This legal action significantly increases the incident's impact and consequences for Unlimited Systems, highlighting the severe repercussions of delayed breach disclosures and the nature of the attack.

articles.headline: ‘RovoBlast’ Flaw in Atlassian AI Enabled One-Click Data Exfiltration
articles.title: DEF CON: Atlassian Rovo AI Flaw Exposed Enterprise Data
articles.excerpt: A critical one-click vulnerability in Atlassian's Rovo enterprise AI assistant, dubbed 'RovoBlast,' could have allowed attackers to steal sensitive data from connected enterprise systems like Jira, Confluence, and SharePoint. Presented at DEF CON by Varonis, the flaw allowed a crafted link to inject malicious prompts into a user's live AI session, tricking the agentic AI into collecting and exfiltrating data. Atlassian has patched the vulnerability.
articles.updateSummary: New details on 'RovoBlast' vulnerability reveal Parameter-to-Prompt (P2P) injection technique and markdown exfiltration method. No in-the-wild exploitation reported.
articles.updateContent: Further analysis of the 'RovoBlast' vulnerability in Atlassian Rovo reveals the specific 'Parameter-to-Prompt (P2P)' injection technique used to bypass traditional jailbreaking. Attackers could leverage markdown image rendering for data exfiltration. The scope of potentially affected platforms is clarified to include Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, in addition to Jira and Confluence. Importantly, despite the critical nature of the flaw, there is currently no evidence of this vulnerability being exploited in the wild, reinforcing that Atlassian's patch was timely and effective. Organizations are reminded to apply least privilege principles to AI agents.

articles.headline: Storm-1175 Exploits N-able Flaw to Deploy StormEncryptor
articles.title: China-Linked Group Hits N-able RMM with New Ransomware
articles.excerpt: The China-linked threat actor Storm-1175 is exploiting a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-18577) in N-able's N-central RMM software. The attacks, which began on August 2, use the flaw as a launchpad for a new custom ransomware strain called 'StormEncryptor,' posing a significant supply-chain risk to managed service providers (MSPs) and their clients. CISA has added the flaw to its KEV catalog.
articles.updateSummary: New TTPs including Mimikatz and Advanced IP Scanner identified in Storm-1175 attacks; N-able releases second hotfix for CVE-2026-18577.
articles.updateContent: Further analysis of Storm-1175's campaign exploiting CVE-2026-18577 reveals additional post-compromise tactics. The threat actor is now observed using Advanced IP Scanner for network discovery and Mimikatz for credential dumping from LSASS process memory. This indicates a more sophisticated approach to lateral movement and persistence within compromised networks. N-able has also released a second hotfix for CVE-2026-18577, emphasizing the critical need for immediate patching to address the authentication bypass vulnerability.

articles.headline: Lazarus Group Exploits Windows Zero-Day in Espionage Campaign
articles.title: Lazarus Group Uses Windows Zero-Day CVE-2026-68820 for SYSTEM-Level Access
articles.excerpt: The North Korean state-sponsored Lazarus Group is actively exploiting a zero-day privilege escalation vulnerability (CVE-2026-68820) in a core Windows driver. The flaw, patched in Microsoft's August 2026 Patch Tuesday, is being used in the 'Operation Dream Job' campaign to deploy a rootkit and target defense and aerospace organizations. Attackers gain SYSTEM privileges to disable security software and conduct espionage.

articles.headline: CISA Warns of Gunra RaaS Targeting Critical Infrastructure
articles.title: CISA Issues Alert on Gunra Ransomware Targeting Global Sectors
articles.excerpt: A joint advisory from CISA, FBI, NSA, and South Korean authorities warns of the Gunra Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS). Derived from leaked Conti source code, the group uses double extortion tactics, targeting critical infrastructure sectors like healthcare and government worldwide. The advisory details TTPs, including exploitation of known vulnerabilities and default credentials, and provides mitigation guidance.

articles.headline: DentaQuest Breach Hits 15M, Largest Health Data Breach of 2026
articles.title: DentaQuest Notifies 15 Million Patients of Massive Data Breach
articles.excerpt: DentaQuest, a major U.S. dental benefits administrator, has disclosed a data breach affecting 15 million individuals, making it the largest healthcare breach of 2026. The data extortion group ShinyHunters claimed responsibility, leaking a 234 GB data archive after ransom negotiations failed. The exposed data includes names, Social Security numbers, and detailed medical and insurance information.

articles.headline: Polish Power Plant Breached via Private Cellular APN Network
articles.title: Hackers Use Private APN to Pivot into Polish Power Plant's OT Network
articles.excerpt: Poland's CERT has detailed a novel cyberattack where intruders breached a power plant's industrial network by pivoting through a private cellular network (APN). The attack, attributed to a Russian state-sponsored group, originated at a compromised wind farm and moved through the shared APN to the power plant, where attackers used default credentials on a PLC to shut down a steam turbine.

articles.headline: Lennar Corp. Discloses Social Engineering Data Breach
articles.title: Homebuilder Lennar Corp. Breach Exposes SSNs via Social Engineering
articles.excerpt: Lennar Corp., a leading U.S. homebuilder, is notifying an undisclosed number of individuals about a data breach that occurred in March 2026. Attackers used 'sophisticated social engineering tactics' to gain access to company systems and exfiltrate sensitive personal data, including names, Social Security numbers, and financial account information. The company discovered the breach in March but only began notifying victims in August.

articles.headline: Oculus Pathology Breach Exposes Patient Data via Email Hack
articles.title: Oculus Pathology Discloses Patient Data Breach from Email Compromise
articles.excerpt: Oculus Pathology, a Texas-based diagnostic services provider, has disclosed a data breach resulting from unauthorized access to employee email accounts in April 2026. The incident potentially exposed a wide range of patient PII and protected health information (PHI), including Social Security numbers, medical diagnoses, and insurance details. The full scope and number of affected individuals are still under investigation.

articles.headline: Aeternum Botnet Uses Polygon Blockchain for Resilient C2
articles.title: Aeternum Botnet Loader Leverages Polygon Smart Contracts
articles.excerpt: A C++ botnet loader named Aeternum is leveraging the public Polygon blockchain for its command-and-control (C2) infrastructure, creating a highly resilient and decentralized threat. Infected devices query public Remote Procedure Call (RPC) endpoints to retrieve commands stored on-chain in smart contracts. This method makes C2 takedowns extremely difficult. The loader also employs anti-evasion techniques, including VM detection. Analysis of the loader reveals a flawed encryption scheme for C2 payloads and its ability to download and execute secondary malware, such as the XMRig cryptominer.
